predictions.experiment: Count of Think-SFT cue answers that hit the 16,384 cap on MATH-500.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. Count rows with cap_hit true, one row per problem_index (if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order). Missing problems (of indices 0-499) count as not cap hits. Report the integer count.
predictions.note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json (committed; read in place, restored from git HEAD into runs/theory-tests/ if absent). 500 rows, 500 unique problem_index 0-499, fields problem_index, score_v3, cap_hit (bool), n_generated (int), so the first-row and missing-problem rules have nothing to act on. Main = rows with cap_hit true. Alt = rows with n_generated >= 16,384 (length at the cap instead of the stored flag; n_generated counts a stop token, so a stopped answer could in principle reach 16,384 too). Caveat: this 'Think-SFT' cell is base + 1.0 x (Think-SFT - base) rebuilt by wsp_edit with nearest rounding (run.json), not the checkpoint loaded directly; prompt is the base's cue prompt, not Think-SFT's native template. refuted_by: count < 28 or > 60.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: share of Think-SFT's wrong answers that are cap hits. The nearest rival (Think-SFT as a uniformly stronger solver on the base's difficulty axis) predicts about the cued base's own share, roughly 0.30 (27 cap hits among about 90 wrong); this theory predicts most wrong answers are cap hits.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, one row per problem_index (first row in file order if repeated). Wrong = score_v3 equal to 0 (or missing or null). Statistic = (number of wrong rows with cap_hit true) / (number of wrong rows). Problems absent from the file are left out of both counts. Report as a fraction.
predictions.note: File: same sft1_cue-01 per_problem.json. Wrong = score_v3 == 0 or missing/null (no nulls in the file; score_v3 is int 0/1). Main = wrong rows with cap_hit true / wrong rows. Alt = treat every cap hit as wrong regardless of score_v3 (grader v3 may extract a boxed answer from a truncated text and mark it right): cap hits / (wrong-by-score union cap hits). If no wrong rows the script reports not_computable (recipe gives no rule for an empty denominator). refuted_by: fraction < 0.50.

predictions.experiment: Share of Think-SFT cap hits that fall in the top quartile of RL's answer length on MATH-500. Random placement gives 0.25.
predictions.recipe: Files studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json and studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, joined on problem_index. Sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500. Statistic = (Think-SFT rows with cap_hit true whose problem is in Q4) / (all Think-SFT rows with cap_hit true). Problems missing from either file are dropped. Report as a fraction.
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (500 rows, t2_generated_tokens int, t2_right int 0/1) and sft1_cue-01 per_problem.json, joined on problem_index (all 500 in both, so nothing dropped). Q4 = 1-based ranks 376-500 after sorting the T1/T2 file's 500 problems by (t2_generated_tokens, problem_index) ascending. Main = SFT cap hits in Q4 / SFT cap hits. Alt = Q4 defined by value: t2_generated_tokens >= the value at rank 376 (all boundary ties included). t2_generated_tokens comes from the rln4 T2 records' n_generated (RL plain, seed base 45,000,000), one sample, so the quartile is a noisy single-draw length. refuted_by: fraction < 0.40.

predictions.experiment: Where Think-SFT's deficit to RL lies: Think-SFT right minus RL (T2) right within the top RL-length quartile.
predictions.recipe: Same join and quartiles as the previous recipe (sort by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties by problem_index, Q4 = ranks 376-500). Within Q4 compute (number of problems with Think-SFT score_v3 = 1) minus (number with t2_right true). A missing or null Think-SFT score counts as 0. Report the signed integer.
predictions.note: Files and Q4 as k=3. Main = (# Q4 problems with Think-SFT score_v3 == 1) - (# Q4 problems with t2_right == 1); missing/null SFT score counts as 0; problems absent from the SFT file are dropped by the join (none are). Alt = same difference with the value-threshold Q4 (boundary ties included), which can hold more than 125 problems. Note the two arms use different prompts (SFT cue, RL plain) and different seeds. refuted_by: difference > +1.

predictions.experiment: Mean generated tokens per problem of Think-SFT cue on MATH-500, against RL plain's 4,694 at the same setting.
predictions.recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, one row per problem_index (first row if repeated). Statistic = arithmetic mean of n_generated over all rows, cap hits included at their stored n_generated. Rows with missing n_generated are dropped. Report in tokens.
predictions.note: File: sft1_cue-01 per_problem.json. Main = mean of stored n_generated over all 500 rows, cap hits at their stored value. Alt = mean of n_new as the job counts it: n_generated - 1 for rows without cap_hit (wsp1_readout notes say n_generated counts the stop token, one more than n_new for an answer that stopped), unchanged for cap hits. The comparison figure 4,694 for RL may be on either convention. refuted_by: mean < 4,700.
